neighbours.label: a big-business entity noun after a size or ranking superlative ('the third largest economy', 'the world's biggest player', 'the leading manufacturer')
fire: Germany remains the largest economy in the European Union by a wide margin.
Toyota became the world's biggest carmaker after overtaking its American rivals.
Nestlé is the largest food company on the planet, with brands in every country.
The group is now the second biggest bank in Brazil after the merger.
Saudi Aramco was briefly the most valuable corporation ever listed.
Shell is one of the largest oil producers operating in the North Sea.
The firm has grown into the leading supplier of microchips for cars.
India is expected to become the third largest economy by the end of the decade.
quiet: Germany has the largest forest in the region by a wide margin.
Toyota launched a new hybrid model after months of testing in the desert.
Grandma's kitchen is the warmest room in the house, with soup on every day.
The group is now the second biggest choir in Brazil after the festival.
The museum owns the most valuable painting ever sold at auction.
Shell collectors spend hours walking the beaches along the North Sea.
The boy has grown into the tallest player on his school team.
India is expected to have very heavy rain by the end of the month.

notes: Card: ' economy', ' corporation', ' player', ' brand', 'mayor' (Spanish 'la mayor operadora') after superlatives. Probe: 'second largest economy' 0.67, 'biggest retailer in' 0.58; plain 'the economy grew' 0.04, 'tallest girl' 0.02. Near misses keep superlatives with non-business nouns, or business nouns without ranking.
